newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tankers steady, W. Africa up slightl.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tankers steady, W. Africa up slightl.

text.p: Middle East crude tanker rates were little changed on Thursday, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) at a steady W67.5 to Japan and to Singapore at around W57.5, brokers said.
"There is business out there but rates really haven't changed much," one said.
He said there continued to be good demand for tonnage to Asia but little interest in voyages west from the Middle East.
Million-barrel ships from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf were slightly firmer at W90-95 from about W87.5 on Wednesday, while VLCCs were steady at W62.5.
"There has been quite good enquiry for 130,000 tonnes from West Africa," another broker said.
Million-barrel vessels from the North Sea to USAC edged up slightly with the West African market to W95 from W92.5, while VLCCs stayed around W62.
U.K./Cont 80,000 tonners rose to W105-W110 from W102.5.
"There's been a lot of action in that sector, with more enquiries and a shortage of vessels until the 28th," a broker said. "It looks like it could move up a bit more."
Cross-Med rates were steady, with million-barrel ships at W95 and 80,000 tonnes at W100-105.
In the Caribbean, rates to the U.S. Gulf firmed for 70,000 tonne ships to W172.5 from W162.5-165.
"There's been bad weather and a number of replacement ships. There are not that many ships out there and when they replace they come in for prompter dates," a U.S. broker said.
Fuel oil was steady at W205 for Caribs-USAC trips.
